name: Griffith Observatory
description: A hilltop observatory with iconic views of the Hollywood Sign and Los Angeles basin. Visit near sunset for a memorable city panorama.

name: Old Los Angeles Zoo
description: Explore mossy abandoned animal enclosures hidden among Griffith Park trees. The old zoo is a wonderfully atmospheric picnic and photo stop.

name: Hollywood Sign Hike
description: A winding trail through Griffith Park leads to broad views behind the Hollywood Sign. Start early for cooler temperatures and clear skies.

name: Bronson Canyon
description: A short canyon walk reaches the Batcave, a film location tucked inside Griffith Park. It is easy to pair with a picnic or nearby hike.

name: Runyon Canyon Park
description: A popular urban hike with open city views and a lively trail culture. The short loop rewards an early start with golden light.

name: Lake Hollywood Park
description: A relaxed lawn with one of the best unobstructed views of the Hollywood Sign. Bring a blanket and stay for the changing afternoon light.

name: Wisdom Tree
description: A solitary pine at the end of a steep trail, marked by a small box of handwritten notes. The overlook feels surprisingly quiet above the city.

name: Hollywood Forever Cemetery
description: A historic cemetery with ornate memorials, gardens, and outdoor film screenings. It is a peaceful place to wander through Los Angeles history.

name: The Getty Center
description: World-class art, architecture, and gardens sit above the Westside with expansive views. Admission is free, making it an easy repeat destination.

name: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
description: LACMA anchors Museum Row with modern and historic collections and its famous Urban Light installation. Plan time for the outdoor art as well as the galleries.

name: Petersen Automotive Museum
description: A dramatic red facade opens into a rotating collection of cars, motorcycles, and design stories. The vault tour adds a deeper look at automotive history.

name: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
description: A cinematic museum exploring filmmaking through costumes, props, and immersive exhibits. The rooftop terrace offers a fresh view over Museum Row.

name: La Brea Tar Pits
description: Active tar seeps and Ice Age fossils make this one of the city’s most unusual outdoor museums. Watch scientists work near the bubbling pits.

name: Hollywood Bowl
description: An open-air amphitheater where music, warm evenings, and picnic tables share the same bowl. Concert nights turn the hills into a glowing backdrop.

name: Grand Central Market
description: A bustling downtown hall packed with tacos, noodles, sandwiches, coffee, and dessert. Go hungry and let the neon signs guide your route.

name: Philippe the Original
description: A century-old counter-service landmark credited with popularizing the French dip sandwich. Sawdust floors and paper menus are part of the charm.

name: Howlin' Rays
description: Nashville hot chicken with a serious heat scale draws lines to Chinatown. The bright, energetic room is as memorable as the sandwich.

name: Smorgasburg LA
description: A Sunday food market at ROW DTLA brings together local chefs, bakers, and makers. It is ideal for grazing with friends and finding a new favorite.

name: Mariscos Jalisco
description: A Boyle Heights food truck famous for crisp shrimp tacos and ceviche tostadas. Arrive early for the freshest batch and a taste of local tradition.

name: Salt & Straw Larchmont
description: Inventive small-batch ice cream flavors make this Larchmont stop a playful dessert destination. Share a flight to sample the seasonal menu.

name: Santa Monica Pier
description: The historic pier stretches over the Pacific with rides, games, and wide sunset views. Walk to the end for the best ocean breeze.

name: Venice Canals
description: Quiet footbridges and small gardens make these canals feel worlds away from the boardwalk. Golden hour reflections are especially lovely.

name: Topanga State Park
description: Oak-shaded trails wind through the Santa Monica Mountains above the coast. The park’s overlooks reveal a surprising amount of ocean and sky.

name: El Matador State Beach
description: Sea caves, rock arches, and steep stairs create a dramatic Malibu shoreline. Visit at low tide and stay for a pastel sunset.

name: Point Dume State Beach
description: A blufftop trail circles a protected cove with seasonal wildflowers and whale-watching views. Descend to the beach for a quieter stretch of sand.

name: Malibu Seafood
description: A casual roadside seafood shack serving fish and chips near the PCH. Eat outside and watch the coastal traffic roll past.

name: The Broad
description: A contemporary art museum downtown known for bold works and its immersive Infinity Mirrored Room. The honeycomb facade is a landmark of Grand Avenue.

name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
description: Frank Gehry’s reflective concert hall rises above downtown with a free public garden on its roof. The curves glow beautifully in late afternoon.

name: Union Station
description: A grand 1939 rail terminal blends Art Deco and Mission Revival details. The waiting room’s leather chairs and tiled courtyards reward a slow wander.

name: Descanso Gardens
description: Botanical collections, oak woodland, and seasonal blooms fill this peaceful foothill garden. The rosarium and Japanese garden are perennial favorites.
